name: Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh + 40 fps cap is the sweet spot for this title — motion feels smooth and the GPU can sustain it with FSR filling in the resolution gap. Drop Shadow Quality or View Distance first if you see sustained dips.

profiles.Summary: Dying Light 2 is a demanding open-world action game that sits right at the Steam Deck's limits — the GPU roughly matches the minimum spec, so expect 30–40 fps at low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling. The game runs well under Proton with full controller support, but high settings or busy outdoor areas will push the hardware hard.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. On your first session, check frame pacing in a large outdoor area like the Bazaar or Garrison rooftops and drop to the Max Battery profile if the Optimal profile stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling with FSR gives the GPU the most headroom; the 8 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock keep thermals and battery draw low. Expect occasional dips below 30 fps in the densest outdoor areas.

KnownIssues: Shader compilation stutters can occur on first play-through of new areas
Ray tracing and DLSS options are unavailable on Linux/Proton — use FSR instead
Large open-world outdoor areas (The Wharf, Garrison rooftops) can cause significant frame dips
In-app purchases / DLC prompts may appear during gameplay

MaxPerformance.Notes: Pushing to 1152x720 with FSR and unlocked TDP gives noticeably better image quality, but the Deck will run warm and battery drains quickly; a stable 60 fps is not realistic in this title at any setting. Reduce View Distance to High → Medium if busy rooftop scenes drop below 35 fps.

Optimal.Notes: Locking the OLED to 40 Hz and capping at 40 fps gives perfectly smooth pacing for the parkour gameplay while allowing medium textures and draw distance for a visually appealing experience. FSR at 1024x640 recovers image quality lost from the lower render resolution.

profiles.Summary: Dying Light 2 Stay Human runs on the Steam Deck at a playable level, but the demanding open-world engine means the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits right at the minimum spec, requiring low settings and FSR upscaling to maintain a stable frame rate. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, and ProtonDB reporters consistently rate it platinum, indicating it launches and plays reliably under Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti class, matching the Deck GPU) and general knowledge of the Chrome Engine's demands. On your first run, check the frame rate in a large outdoor area with many zombies — if it dips below your target, drop to the next profile down or reduce View Distance and Shadow Quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU load low enough for the 8 W TDP cap to hold 30 fps through most of the open world. Disable motion blur and depth of field first — they are the biggest free-performance wins on Deck.

KnownIssues: Shader compilation stutters can occur early in a session until the shader cache is fully built
The game's built-in motion blur and depth of field can cause additional GPU overhead and should be disabled on Deck
Open-world areas with dense zombie hordes or large draw distances can cause frame rate dips below target
Ray tracing options (if exposed) must be kept off entirely, as the Deck GPU cannot handle them

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at native 1280x800 with medium settings and full TDP pushes the Deck to its limit; expect occasional dips into the high-30s during the most demanding outdoor scenes with large zombie crowds. Battery life is short at 15 W TDP, so this profile is best for docked or short sessions.
